site: Any employer ATS account-creation form (found by the REA evidence audit of 23 October)
class: A site's rule for the password being chosen was read as a refusal of the owner's password
symptom: On a create-account form the message 'Password is invalid: must include at least one symbol' was classified wrong_password, the state that leads to resetting a password by emailed code.
root_cause: account_state.read_state matched 'password is invalid' in any page text and ranked it above the form-error and account-exists readings, without asking whether the page was making an account (no password of the owner's had been tried) or signing in.
why_tests_missed: State tests used sign-in pages for wrong-password wording and create pages for form errors; none put the invalid-password wording on a create form.
fix: On a page that makes an account (two password boxes, or a create heading) the bare phrase 'password is/was/are invalid' and 'invalid password' no longer count as a credential refusal; explicit evidence (wrong or incorrect credentials, locked, already registered, a Sign In heading) keeps its meaning. Replayed over 833 saved pages: no reading changed.
prevention: Decide which step a page is (create, sign in, verify) before reading what its messages mean; a validation message about a value being chosen never triggers recovery of a value the owner supplied.
